From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Neha — quick technical readout and proposed controls. I reviewed the medspan_sla_draft_v1.pdf and ran a simulation on ms-alpha-v0 characteristics on our staging fleet. Summary:

- Risk: ms-alpha-v0 is ~25% higher p95 latency under cold-cache and multi-request bursts vs ms-stable-v2. CPU/GPU memory pressure increases during the first 10–20 minutes of sustained traffic as the KV cache stabilizes.
- Mitigations we can implement (fast):
  1) Canary routing: start at 2% traffic, ramp to 10% over 48h, then to 30% if metrics stable. Canary will use separate instance pool (so it won't affect stable capacity).
  2) Auto-fallback rule: if p95 > 400ms over a 5-minute window or error-rate >1% over 2m, route traffic to ms-stable-v2.
  3) Grace-window logic: exclude incidents that are <10 minutes of continuous elevated latency from SLA calculations during the 30-day alpha period. We log and surface them in a dedicated dashboard.
  4) Monitoring: we can spin up a shared Grafana view and a dedicated telemetry stream to MedSpan (read-only link). Delivery ETA: within 12 hours if we prioritize.

Operational caveats: fallback to stable model will change results for some user-facing queries; the customer must accept that behavior during the window. Also, prolonged warm-up periods may cause higher token-costs for the pilot — budget should be considered.

Proposed temporary SLA language to present to legal (short form):
- Alpha grace period: 30 calendar days from pilot launch. During this period, Redwood will not count as SLA violations any single incident of elevated latency or partial availability lasting less than 10 consecutive minutes, provided automated fallback policies were in place and enabled.
- Monitoring: Redwood will provide a read-only dashboard link and daily summary emails for the pilot.

If leadership signs off, I can prepare the routing policy and the Grafana link today.

— Dev Patel
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for the quick read and the draft. We can support MedSpan's request with a formal, timeboxed approach. Proposed agreement (high level) for the pilot:

- Scope: ms-alpha-v0 only; applies for a single 30-day alpha window starting at pilot launch.
- Exceptions: incidents under 10 consecutive minutes of elevated latency or partial availability will be excluded from SLA breach calculations during the window, provided Redwood's auto-fallback and canary routing are enabled.
- Fallback: auto-route to ms-stable-v2 if p95 > 400ms over 5 minutes or error-rate >1% over 2 minutes.
- Rollout: begin at 2% traffic, ramp to 10% over 48 hours; require customer sign-off to exceed 30% traffic during alpha.
- Monitoring: we'll provide a read-only Grafana link and daily digest emails; we will also create a shared incident channel for rapid triage.

Next steps I propose:
1) MedSpan legal: review the brief amendment language in the attached draft and mark any non-starters.
2) Redwood: we'll prepare the canary/routing policy and the Grafana link (Dev to deliver within 12 hours once we have sign-off).
3) Both sides: sign DocuSign amendment (I will upload a short amendment to the HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/MS-2026-4321).

If that sounds workable I will escalate for an operational sign-off from Marcus and a one-line leadership approval from Grace to proceed.

Thanks — I know the timeline is tight; we will move fast.
